name: Ministral 3 (8B and 14B, Instruct and Reasoning, 2512)

official_org.value: Mistral AI. The HF org 'mistralai' is verified (isVerified=true, fullname 'Mistral', 83 models). The vendor blog 'Introducing Mistral 3' and the model cards link to each other.

release_date.value: Public release 2025-12-02: the mistral.ai/news/mistral-3 page has datePublished 2025-12-02T16:00:00Z, the ggml-org GGUFs were created 2025-12-02, and Artificial Analysis lists releaseDate 2025-12-02. The HF createdAt of the main repos is 2025-10-31 (14B-Reasoning 08:42:28Z, 14B-Instruct 08:43:24Z, 8B-Reasoning 08:41:36Z, 8B-Instruct 08:43:35Z). Those repos were created while still private. The repos were last modified 2026-07-15. The paper is arXiv 2601.08584 (2026-01-13). The 2025-12-02 release falls inside 2025-11-15..2026-11-15.

license.value: apache-2.0 (card tag 'license: apache-2.0'). The card text says 'Open-source license allowing usage and modification for both commercial and non-commercial purposes' and adds only 'You must not use this model in a manner that infringes ... any third party's rights'. There is no use-based restriction and no gating (gated=false in the API).

params.value: Both sizes are dense, so all parameters are active. 14B: the card says 13.5B language model plus 0.4B vision encoder; the HF API safetensors total is 13,945,031,680. 8B: the card says 8.4B LM plus 0.4B vision; the API total is 8,918,026,240. The Instruct repos store weights in FP8: 14B has 12.16B F8_E4M3 plus 1.78B BF16, 8B has 7.42B F8_E4M3 plus 1.50B BF16. The Reasoning repos are pure BF16.

architecture.value: The class is Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration (model_type mistral3; the text model is ministral3) with a Pixtral vision tower: 24 layers, hidden 1024, 0.4B parameters. 14B text: 40 layers, hidden 5120, FFN 16384, 32 query heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, vocab 131072, untied embeddings. 8B text: 34 layers, hidden 4096, FFN 14336, 32 query heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128. Every layer uses full GQA attention (sliding_window null). There are no Mamba, linear or MLA layers. RoPE is YaRN with factor 16 over an original 16384 (plus llama_4_scaling beta 0.1); rope_theta is 1e9 on the 14B and 1e6 on the 8B. The paper describes 'Cascade Distillation' (pruning plus distillation).

context_length.value: 262144 tokens (max_position_embeddings 262144; YaRN factor 16 x original 16384). The card says 'Supports a 256k context window'. Ollama lists 256K.

modalities.value: Input is text plus images; output is text. Text-only paths exist: vLLM v0.33.0 has --language-model-only, which the vLLM recipe lists as 'text_only: Skip loading the vision encoder ... frees VRAM for KV cache'. In llama.cpp, leave out the mmproj file (--no-mmproj). No text-only checkpoint exists from Mistral; one community build does (ppetermann/Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512-textonly-NVFP4, unverified).

thinking.how_to_toggle: There is no per-request switch. Thinking is chosen by variant: the *-Reasoning-2512 models think, the *-Instruct-2512 models do not. Neither chat template has an enable_thinking or reasoning_effort kwarg. In the Reasoning template, a default system prompt ('# HOW YOU SHOULD THINK AND ANSWER ... [THINK]...[/THINK]') is inserted ONLY when the first message is not a system message. OpenCode always sends its own system prompt, so the card's advice applies: append SYSTEM_PROMPT.txt (the THINK instructions) to your custom system prompt, or the model may not think. vLLM: --reasoning-parser mistral puts the [THINK] text into the 'reasoning' field. The card recommends keeping reasoning traces in multi-turn context; the template accepts reasoning/reasoning_content on assistant turns. llama.cpp: a dedicated Ministral 3 handler (common/parsers/ministral3.cpp) extracts [THINK]...[/THINK] when reasoning_format is not none. Ollama: the library has Instruct tags only, so there is no thinking. Recommended sampling: Reasoning temperature 1.0 (card) or 0.7/top_p 0.95 (card examples); Instruct temperature below 0.1.

tool_calling.format: Mistral v13 tekken control tokens: [AVAILABLE_TOOLS]<json>[/AVAILABLE_TOOLS] in the prompt, and output [TOOL_CALLS]name[ARGS]{json} (no [CALL_ID]), with results in [TOOL_RESULTS].
tool_calling.evidence: Both the Instruct and Reasoning chat_template.jinja render tools: "set available_tools = '[AVAILABLE_TOOLS]' + (tools|tojson) + '[/AVAILABLE_TOOLS]'", which is emitted before the last user turn. The card says 'Agentic: Offers best-in-class agentic capabilities with native function calling and JSON outputting'. The card serve commands use --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser mistral. The paper says tool execution was enabled during online preference optimisation, and the reasoning SFT data includes tool use. The official GGUFs embed the same template (6206 chars; it contains [SYSTEM_PROMPT], [TOOL_CALLS] and [ARGS] but no [CALL_ID]), which matches llama.cpp's detection rule for its Ministral 3 handler.

FP8 E4M3, static activation scale (vision tower, projector and lm_head kept in BF16); HF shards 15.73 GB = 14.65 GiB
FP8 E4M3 static; HF shards 10.42 GB = 9.70 GiB
GGUF Q8_0 14.36 GB + mmproj Q8_0 0.47 GB
GGUF Q8_0 14.36 GB + mmproj Q8_0 0.47 GB
NVFP4 W4A4 (llm-compressor). Only the MLPs are FP4; attention, embeddings, lm_head and vision stay BF16 (read from the safetensors header). Single consolidated.safetensors of 13.42 GB = 12.50 GiB

vllm.arch_supported: Yes. At tag v0.33.0, vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py line 541 maps 'Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration' to (mistral3, Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration), and line 178 maps 'Ministral3ForCausalLM' to MistralForCausalLM. --language-model-only exists in v0.33.0 arg_utils.py (line 1497).
vllm.min_version: Card: vllm >= 0.12.0 with mistral_common >= 1.8.6. The vLLM recipe says min_vllm_version 0.11.0. v0.33.0 is fine.
vllm.best_checkpoint: Thinking: cyankiwi/Ministral-3-14B-Reasoning-2512-AWQ-4bit (9.68 GiB, W4A16 Marlin), or the 8B Reasoning AWQ for more context. No thinking: the official mistralai/Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512 (FP8, 9.70 GiB). The official 14B Instruct FP8 (14.65 GiB) and the 14B BF16 checkpoints do NOT fit.
vllm.serve_command:
8B Instruct (official FP8, no thinking): docker run --gpus all --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface -e VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0 mistralai/Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512 --tokenizer-mode mistral --config-format mistral --load-format mistral --language-model-only --max-model-len 65536 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser mistral --served-model-name ministral-3-8b-instruct
14B Reasoning (community AWQ, thinking): docker run --gpus all --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0 cyankiwi/Ministral-3-14B-Reasoning-2512-AWQ-4bit --tokenizer-mode mistral --language-model-only --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --max-model-len 65536 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser mistral --reasoning-parser mistral --served-model-name ministral-3-14b-reasoning
(The card and recipe base command is: vllm serve <repo> --tokenizer_mode mistral --config_format mistral --load_format mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser mistral [--reasoning-parser mistral].)
vllm.reasoning_parser: mistral (v0.33.0 vllm/reasoning/__init__.py line 139: 'mistral' -> MistralParserReasoningAdapter, built on vllm/parser/mistral.py, which detects [THINK] special tokens for v13+ tokenizers)
vllm.quant_on_sm120: In the v0.33.0 source, W4A16 compressed-tensors (AWQ-style) runs on MarlinLinearKernel, whose get_min_capability is 75, so sm_120 is supported (inferred from source). FP8 static (the official Instruct) runs on the FP8 scaled-mm path; open issue #55571 reports Xid 13 / illegal memory access on SM120 under sustained FP8 load with FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel, and VLLM_DISABLED_KERNELS=FlashInferFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel avoids it. NVFP4 (RedHatAI) would use the SM120 FP4 kernels but leaves only about 1.8 GiB for KV cache.
vllm.kv_math:
Budget 16303 MiB x 0.92 = 14999 MiB = 14.65 GiB; reserve 1.2 GiB. KV per token, BF16: 14B = 2 x 40 layers x 8 x 128 x 2 = 163,840 B (160 KiB); 8B = 2 x 34 x 8 x 128 x 2 = 139,264 B (136 KiB). FP8 KV halves both. All layers are full attention, so cost is linear in context.
- 8B Instruct FP8 official, 9.70 GiB: KV pool 3.74 GiB, giving 28.8k (BF16) / 57.7k (FP8). With --language-model-only (minus about 0.80 GiB vision): 4.54 GiB, giving 35.0k / 70.0k.
- 8B Reasoning AWQ, 6.69 GiB: 6.76 GiB, giving 52.1k / 104.2k. Language-only: 7.56 GiB, giving 58.3k / 116.5k.
- 14B Reasoning or Instruct AWQ, 9.68 GiB: 3.77 GiB, giving 24.7k / 49.4k. Language-only (minus 0.82): 4.59 GiB, giving 30.1k / 60.1k. At gpu-mem-util 0.95 (15.13 GiB) and language-only: 5.07 GiB, giving about 33k / 66k.
- 14B NVFP4 RedHat, 12.50 GiB: 0.95 GiB, giving 6.2k / 12.4k. Language-only: 1.77 GiB, giving 11.6k / 23.2k.
- 14B Instruct FP8 official, 14.65 GiB: does not fit (pool -1.2 GiB; -0.38 GiB language-only).
- 14B or 8B Reasoning BF16 (25.97 / 16.61 GiB): does not fit.
vllm.known_issues:
Open vLLM issues:
- #53481 (open, mistral label): the FLASHINFER attention backend gives degenerate output for Mistral3 on sm_120 (reproduced on an RTX 5090) with any KV dtype. Forcing --kv-cache-dtype fp8 removes FLASH_ATTN from the candidates, so auto-selection lands on FlashInfer. The workaround is --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN. Fix PR #53754 is still unmerged.
- #48945 (open): 'Ministral is broken with --kv-cache-dtype fp8' (the same root cause).
- #66113 (open, 2026-11-06): Ministral-3 FP8 with --config-format hf builds the vision tower as FP8, so image embeddings are zero. Use the mistral config format, or --language-model-only.
- #64309 (open): thinking_token_budget never triggers for [THINK] Mistral models.
- #67520 (open, 2026-11-13): mistral parser tests fail on main after tool_choice=None was normalised to 'none'; it is a main-branch regression, so check v0.34.
- #58145 (open): the Mistral grammar path rebuilds the tool parser on the event loop on every request (a latency cost).
- #55571 (open): FP8 Xid on SM120 (see above).
Closed: #29968 (streaming tool calls), #40318 (text-only startup).

llamacpp.arch_supported: Yes. llama.cpp src/llama-arch.cpp at b12418 has LLM_ARCH_MISTRAL3 'mistral3', and the official GGUF header reads general.architecture=mistral3. A dedicated chat handler, common/parsers/ministral3.cpp, is selected in common/chat.cpp line 1271 when the template has [SYSTEM_PROMPT], [TOOL_CALLS] and [ARGS] but no [CALL_ID]. It handles [THINK] reasoning, parallel tool calls and a lazy grammar triggered on [TOOL_CALLS]. tests/test-chat.cpp tests the models/templates/mistralai-Ministral-3-14B-Reasoning-2512.jinja template. b12418 (2026-11-15) is marked prerelease, like every bNNNN build.
llamacpp.quant: Q4_K_M (7.67 GiB). Q5_K_M (8.96 GiB) fits about 64k only just. For the 8B, Q8_0 (8.41 GiB).
llamacpp.offload_plan: Everything on the GPU (-ngl 99). The model is dense, so --n-cpu-moe does not apply. Leave out mmproj for text-only use. VRAM = GGUF + q8_0 KV (14B: 160 KiB x 34/64 = 85 KiB/token; 8B: 72.25 KiB/token) + about 0.8 GiB compute. 14B Q4_K_M: 32k 11.1 GiB, 64k 13.8 GiB, 80k about 15.1 GiB (tight), 96k 16.4 GiB (no). 14B Q5_K_M at 64k: 15.1 GiB (tight). 14B Q8_0 at 32k: 16.8 GiB (no). 8B Q8_0 at 64k: 13.7 GiB. 8B Q4_K_M at 128k: 14.7 GiB. With F16 KV, 14B Q4_K_M at 64k needs 18.5 GiB (no), so q8_0 KV is required.
llamacpp.server_command: docker run --gpus all -p 8080:8080 -v ~/models:/models ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda13 -m /models/Ministral-3-14B-Reasoning-2512-Q4_K_M.gguf --jinja -ngl 99 -c 65536 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --temp 0.7 --top-p 0.95 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --alias ministral-3-14b-reasoning  (for the Instruct GGUF, use --temp 0.1)
llamacpp.tool_calling_note: --jinja (on by default) uses the embedded template. The official GGUF embeds the full 6206-char template with [AVAILABLE_TOOLS], [TOOL_CALLS] and [ARGS] and no [CALL_ID], so the dedicated Ministral 3 PEG parser is used: tool calls come back as OpenAI tool_calls, and reasoning comes back in reasoning_content. Not tested end to end on this machine.

ollama.tag: ministral-3:14b (= 14b-instruct-2512-q4_K_M); also ministral-3:8b / latest (8b-instruct-2512-q4_K_M), plus q8_0 and fp16 tags
ollama.context: The library lists 256K. Ollama's default num_ctx is 4k on GPUs under 24 GiB, so set num_ctx to 65536 or more for OpenCode.
ollama.capabilities: Badges: vision and tools. There is no thinking badge and no Reasoning variant in the library. Sizes: 14b q4_K_M 9.1 GB, 14b q8_0 15 GB, 14b fp16 28 GB, 8b q4_K_M 6.0 GB, 8b q8_0 9.9 GB, 8b fp16 18 GB. The page says 'Updated 11 months ago' and shows 1.6M downloads.

speed_notes: Inferred bandwidth ceilings use 896 GB/s divided by the bytes read per token; the model is dense, so all weights are read for every token. 14B Q4_K_M (8.24 GB) gives a ceiling of about 109 tok/s, roughly 65-80 tok/s in practice. 14B AWQ in vLLM (about 9.5 GB of language-model weights) gives about 94 tok/s. 8B Instruct FP8 (about 9.6 GB without vision) gives about 94 tok/s. 8B AWQ (about 6.3 GB) gives about 140 tok/s. 8B Q8_0 (9.03 GB) gives about 99 tok/s. TRITON_ATTN, which is required for FP8 KV on sm_120, was reported in vLLM #53481 as having 'no decode cost vs the healthy backends' (64-67 tok/s on the 3B on an RTX PRO card). There are no measured RTX 5080 numbers. Artificial Analysis API speeds (Mistral's cloud, not local) are 73 tok/s for the 14B and 83 tok/s for the 8B. Prefill of 30-60k-token OpenCode prompts on a 14B dense model will take several seconds per cold turn; prefix caching helps.

opencode_fit.recommended_runtime: llama.cpp (server-cuda13) with the official GGUF; vLLM v0.33.0 is the alternative for the 8B Instruct FP8 or the 14B Reasoning AWQ, with --language-model-only, FP8 KV and --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN
opencode_fit.recommended_checkpoint: Thinking: mistralai/Ministral-3-14B-Reasoning-2512-GGUF Q4_K_M. No thinking: mistralai/Ministral-3-14B-Instruct-2512-GGUF Q4_K_M. In vLLM, mistralai/Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512 (FP8) or cyankiwi/Ministral-3-14B-Reasoning-2512-AWQ-4bit.
opencode_fit.recommended_context: 64k (65536) with q8_0/FP8 KV. About 80k is the ceiling for the 14B Q4_K_M in llama.cpp; the 8B Q4_K_M reaches about 128k.
opencode_fit.caveats:
1. Independent agentic scores are low: AA Terminal-Bench 2.1 is 9.7% (14B) and 4.1% (8B), and tau2 is about 27%. Mistral publishes no SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench or BFCL numbers. This is a general edge model, not a coding agent; Devstral is Mistral's coding line.
2. Thinking can only be switched by choosing the variant, never per request. OpenCode's system prompt replaces the template's default THINK system prompt, so append SYSTEM_PROMPT.txt or the Reasoning model may answer without thinking.
3. vLLM on sm_120: FP8 KV auto-selects the FlashInfer backend, which gives garbage for Mistral3 (#53481/#48945 open), so --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN is mandatory. BF16 KV auto-selects FLASH_ATTN and works.
4. The official 14B Instruct FP8 (14.65 GiB) does not fit in vLLM.
5. The card asks for Instruct temperature below 0.1 and Reasoning temperature 0.7-1.0; set this per model in OpenCode.
6. OpenCode v2.3.0's vLLM discovery starts models with tools disabled; enable capabilities.tools by hand.
7. Ollama has Instruct only, with a 4k default context.

gaps: No vendor-reported SWE-bench Verified/Pro, Terminal-Bench, BFCL, tau2 or Aider numbers exist for any Ministral 3 variant; independent AA numbers cover only the non-reasoning (Instruct) entries, and the AA page for 'ministral-3-14b-reasoning' returns 404.

The AA Intelligence Index value (about 10.0 for the 14B) came from embedded page JSON; the rendered page shows 'Unknown' for the current index version, so the version that value belongs to is unclear.
No measured RTX 5080 / sm_120 throughput for Ministral 3 8B or 14B; speed figures are bandwidth arithmetic only.

I did not confirm that the community AWQ checkpoints (cyankiwi) load cleanly in v0.33.0 with --tokenizer-mode mistral and the HF config format, or that the duplicate consolidated.safetensors is skipped by the default loader; the quality loss of the AWQ builds is not published.
Did not verify whether the Reasoning model still emits [THINK] without the THINK system prompt (OpenCode supplies its own system prompt); behaviour is inferred from the template and card guidance.

Did not verify the llama.cpp reasoning-budget or no-think behaviour for this handler, or whether Ollama can run the mistralai Reasoning GGUFs via hf.co/ pulls (architecture mistral3 support in Ollama's engine not checked).
Per-file sizes for the unsloth, bartowski and lmstudio-community GGUF repos were not pulled; the official mistralai GGUFs were used for the arithmetic.
The vLLM recipe references mistralai/Ministral-3-14B-Instruct-2512-FP8, which does not exist in the HF API listing (recipe error).
OpenCode v2.3.0 interplay with the mistral tool parser (tool_choice omitted, issue #60202; tool-call ID format) was not tested.
